text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High rate of 429s for tenant `zenhealth` in VPC-dedicated pool eu-west-1. Error surge started ~10:12 UTC, 5xx low, 429s spiking. Auto-mitigation attempted (burst fallback) but showing repeated rejections. Paging SRE oncall.

maria-sre: acked. I'm taking. @alex-sre FYI this looks customer-impacting — ZenHealth reporting degraded service in production. Can we get tenant-level view and recent deploys?

alex-sre: on it. Checking pool metrics and token-bucket logs. ZenHealth is on DedicatedPool-zen-eu1. No new deploys to the pool in last 24h per deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: no deploys: commit 9f3a2e8 to runtime-service rolled 3 days ago. CI checks green.

nate-csm: adding context from customer: ZenHealth says "sudden 429s for all API keys, some calls succeed intermittently". They are on enterprise contract with higher limits (agreed 3x standard). They called support desk, asking for emergency override.

kelly-ops: can we confirm whether limit hit is at the per-tenant quota layer or per-key? Logs I pulled show token_bucket_exhausted entries with tenant=zenhealth. Example log snippet:

```
2026-03-14T10:11:52Z rate_limiter WARN token_bucket_exhausted tenant=zenhealth limit=2500/s consumed=2501
2026-03-14T10:12:10Z proxy 429 tenant=zenhealth route=/v1/generate status=429
```

chris-runtime: adding: latency and GPU utilization on DedicatedPool-zen-eu1 are normal. KV cache hit rates are stable. This suggests policy/ratelimiter regression or a sudden traffic pattern spike (many small concurrent sessions).

maria-sre: taking immediate triage steps: 1) verify scope (tenant vs route) 2) open contract-override request 3) apply temporary emergency lift for 15m while we investigate fallback. Proposed emergency action: temporary tenant override to bypass quota check for zenhealth for 15 minutes (audit log + manual rollback). Anyone object?

raj-oncall: +1 for emergency lift. Need to ensure we have audit trail and that SDK tokens can't go wild. Suggest we cap burst concurrency to avoid runaway cost by combining override with a request cap: allow bypass of rate_limit but enforce hard concurrency=200 per-tenant.

alex-sre: how-to: we have an admin API for overrides. Example command:

```
# emergency override: grant zenhealth unlimited for 15m (audit=true)
redwoodctl admin quota override --tenant zenhealth --scope tenant --action lift --duration 15m --reason "customer emergency: 429s"
```

maria-sre: executing now. I will also add a concurrency cap:

```
redwoodctl admin quota set --tenant zenhealth --concurrency 200 --persist false
```

maria-sre: (running) ...

maria-sre: override response: OK override_id=ovr_78b3, expires=2026-03-14T10:27:00Z. Concurrency cap applied. Audit log entry created.

nate-csm: passed to customer: "we applied a temporary lift and a concurrency cap — please confirm if traffic normalizes. We'll monitor and follow-up with a formal contract check." They replied: some calls are coming through, error rate dropping.

chris-runtime: seeing immediate drop in 429s from ~18% -> 4% over 2 minutes. GPU and pool metrics stable. KV cache fine. We'll keep an eye.

kelly-ops: opened internal ticket CH-2321 for contract verification and billing update. Noting this was an emergency lift; legal/finance must approve any permanent quota change. Assigning to finance for review.

alex-sre: can we capture a sample of requests that were previously rejected to understand pattern? Suggest capture N=500 rejected logs and paste to secure storage. I'll run a query now.

alex-sre: query results: spikes were correlated with many small streaming sessions (~120-300 tokens each) from the same set of client IPs over a short window. Candidate explanation: a client-side retry loop or bot.

maria-sre: I'll add a temporary WAF rule to slow or block abusive IPs in addition to the concurrency cap. Blocking rule applied: `block ip set [10.4.12.0/24, 52.88.99.45]` (internal network alias used for display). Monitoring.

deploy-bot: incident annotation: override_id=ovr_78b3 applied by maria-sre; concurrency cap set; waf_patch_id=waf_402.

nate-csm: customer confirms: they had a background job that re-introduced a fanout pattern — they've paused it. Will follow up with engineering changes on their side.

maria-sre: next steps: 1) keep override active until root cause verified and customer confirms fix 2) prepare rollback plan (automatic expiry in 15m + manual revoke if issues) 3) collect logs and write post-incident note. I'm handing to night oncall @raj-oncall at 10:25 UTC. If anything changes escalate back to primary SRE.

raj-oncall: taking over. I'll monitor metrics and chat with nate in 15m to confirm customer-side changes. Please drop any artifacts (queries, captures) here.

alex-sre: artifacts uploaded to secure bucket: s3://prod-incident-logs/zenhealth/1753456789/rejected-samples.log

maria-sre: adding timeline + notes to incident ticket CH-2321. Will draft postmortem skeleton after we confirm full resolution.

kelly-ops: finance ping: we need to track any overage exposure due to lift. Tagging billing team and adding budget alert.

nate-csm: customer says error rate ~down to normal. They will keep their job paused and coordinate an internal fix. Thanks team.

maria-sre: override expired automatically at 10:27 UTC (as scheduled). Re-checking 429 rate now.

chris-runtime: 429s remain low (~2%). No regression after expiry. Looks stable.

raj-oncall: keeping monitoring for 1h, then will close incident if no recurrence. Closing checklist: confirm customer-reported fix, confirm logs captured, handoff update to CSM and billing.

nate-csm: will coordinate with ZenHealth to schedule safe ramp and run controlled load test later today.

maria-sre: post-incident actions (assigned): SRE to analyze rate-limiter thresholds and pattern (maria-sre, alex-sre), Runtime to verify pool sizing and fallback config (chris-runtime), CSM to follow up on customer fix and contract (nate-csm), Finance to review billing exposure (kelly-ops). I'll create Jira CH-2330 for the deep-dive.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: status=mitigated severity=high impact=partial tenant=zenhealth notes="temporary override + concurrency cap + WAF block; customer paused offending job". Incident channel closed for updates.
